report.source_text: A cranial contrast enhanced MRI was conducted the following month, revealing an entirely altered optic nerve affecting the retrobulbar, prechiasmal, and optic chiasm level. A pathological, smoothly contoured mass with cystic changes was described and measured about 5.2 cm × 2.0 cm × 1.9 cm. Greater peripheral contrast accumulation in the pathological tissue extended along the optic chiasm and relatively close to the frontal lobe’s straight gyrus. The pathological mass also extended relatively close to the A1 segment of the anterior cerebral artery and stretched in the direction of the pituitary gland. A lateral depression of the extraocular muscles was also noted (Figure 4). The contrast-enhancing component of the tumor on diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) sequence showed a restricted diffusion at an apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) value of 1500 × 10−6 mm2/s, with a b value of 1000 s/mm2. A high T2 signal intensity was also noted.

report.source_text: Thorough histopathological analyses highlighted the moderate formation of cellular material, consisting of spherical cells with pronounced nuclear polymorphism, multinucleated tumor cells, and an area of vascular proliferation (Figure 7). Multiple mitotic figures were visualized within the tissue. A histochemical analysis of the tumor tissue revealed the presence of positive glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP). Alpha thalassemia intellectual disability syndrome X-linked (ATRX) and isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 (IDH 1 R132H) were both negative. Antigen Kiel 67 protein (KI-67) was positive, but not elevated, around 20–25%.

clinician.final_diagnosis: a diagnosis of glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, WHO Classification Grade 4
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 68-year-old woman presented with six months of painless left eye proptosis, deteriorating eyesight, limited upward gaze, and partial vision loss. A cranial contrast-enhanced MRI revealed a large (5.2 cm × 2.0 cm × 1.9 cm) pathological mass with cystic changes, affecting the optic nerve, prechiasmal, and optic chiasm levels, extending towards the frontal lobe, showing peripheral contrast accumulation, restricted diffusion, and high T2 signal intensity. Histopathological and immunohistochemical examination of the biopsy confirmed a diagnosis of glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, WHO Classification Grade 4, characterized by moderate cellularity, pronounced nuclear polymorphism, multinucleated tumor cells, vascular proliferation, multiple mitotic figures, positive glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), negative Alpha thalassemia intellectual disability syndrome X-linked (ATRX) and isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 (IDH 1 R132H), and Antigen Kiel 67 protein (KI-67) positive at 20–25%. Postoperatively, the patient developed full blindness of the left eye, oculomotor nerve paresis, left-sided ptosis, and no major change in exophthalmos. Postoperative head MRI showed partial resection of the left optic nerve with residual tumor tissue and edema.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with painless outward protrusion of the left eye, deteriorating eyesight, limited upward gaze, and partial vision loss in the left eye.

Cranial contrast-enhanced MRI revealed a large (5.2 cm × 2.0 cm × 1.9 cm) pathological mass with cystic changes, affecting the optic nerve, prechiasmal, and optic chiasm levels, extending towards the frontal lobe, showing peripheral contrast accumulation, restricted diffusion, and high T2 signal intensity.

Histopathological analyses of the tumor tissue highlighted moderate cellularity, spherical cells with pronounced nuclear polymorphism, multinucleated tumor cells, vascular proliferation, multiple mitotic figures, positive glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), negative Alpha thalassemia intellectual disability syndrome X-linked (ATRX) and isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 (IDH 1 R132H), and Antigen Kiel 67 protein (KI-67) positive at 20–25%.
Histopathological and immunohistochemical examination findings revealed a diagnosis of glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, WHO Classification Grade 4.
After the operation, full blindness of the left eye, oculomotor nerve paresis, left sided ptosis, and no major change in the exophthalmos were noted.

Postoperative head MRI showed partial resection of the left optic nerve. Residual tumor tissue and edema were noted in the left retrobulbar space, extending into the left prechiasmal space and into the left side of the optic chiasm.
